text:
For a typical full-size fridge, get a power station with **at least 1,000 Wh of capacity and an inverter rated 1,200–1,500 W or more**. Pick about 2,000 Wh if you want a full day or more of backup.

**The numbers to size by**
- **Running power:** A full-size fridge draws about 100–200 W while the compressor runs. The compressor cycles on and off, so the average over a day is closer to 50–70 W. ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/))
- **Startup surge:** The compressor can briefly pull about 1,000–1,200 W when it kicks on. The power station's inverter has to handle that, so inverter rating matters as much as capacity. Units under about 500 Wh often can't start a compressor. ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/))
- **Daily energy:** Expect roughly 1–1.7 kWh per day. HomeGrid HQ's own figures aren't fully consistent, and Anker's example of a 70 W average works out to about 1,680 Wh per day (my arithmetic).

**Rough sizing by outage length**

| Outage | Capacity | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| A few hours up to about half a day | ~1,000 Wh | Estimated at 10–20 hours, depending on the fridge |
| About 1 day | ~2,000 Wh | Anker claims up to 35 hours for its 2,010 Wh model in controlled testing |
| Multi-day | 4,000 Wh or more, or add solar | |

**Example models**
- **Anker SOLIX S2000** has 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W continuous output and 3,000 W peak. It's a good match for about a day of fridge backup. [Anker SOLIX guide](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator)
- **BLUETTI AC200L** is listed at $899. With code AFF5OFF it was $854.05 in BLUETTI's cart on 2026-10-21. I didn't read the product page, so check its capacity and inverter rating against the numbers above before buying. [Deal link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (1,070 Wh) is estimated at about 17 hours. **EcoFlow Delta 3 Max** (2,048 Wh) is estimated at about 33 hours. **EcoFlow Delta Pro 3** (4,096 Wh) is estimated at about 2.8 days. These are HomeGrid HQ's estimates. I don't have purchase links for these.

**Tips**
- Check your fridge's nameplate or EnergyGuide label for its actual wattage. Chest freezers and mini fridges use less.
- Keep the doors closed during the outage. This stretches runtime and keeps food cold.
- Test the fridge on the power station before an outage, since the startup surge is what trips undersized units.
- Runtime estimates assume about 85% inverter efficiency. Real results vary with kitchen temperature and fridge age.

If you tell me your fridge's size or wattage and how long an outage you want to cover, I can narrow this down.

fetched.result:
**Fridge power needs (from the page)**

- **Running watts:** About 80W for a mini fridge, 120W for an 18 cu ft top-freezer, 180W for a 25 cu ft French door, and 100W for a garage chest freezer. Modern full-size fridges draw roughly 100-200W while the compressor runs.
- **Startup surge:** About 600W for a mini fridge, 1,000W for a top-freezer, 1,200W for a French door, and 800W for a chest freezer. The page says the surge is the number that matters most for choosing an inverter.
- **Daily energy:** The page gives a 35% duty cycle, which works out to about 62Wh per hour after inverter losses, or roughly 1.5kWh per day (my calculation). The page also says the average over a day is 30-50W, so its figures are not fully consistent.

**Recommended capacity**

- **Minimum inverter:** At least 1,200W of surge, and the page says any 1kWh-class unit with a 1,500W+ inverter handles a typical fridge.
- **Battery size:** About 1,000Wh covers most of a day, 2,000Wh about a day and a third, and 4,000Wh or more covers a multi-day outage.
- **Small units:** Sub-500Wh units often cannot start the compressor.

**Runtime examples (page estimates)**

| Power station | Capacity | Est. runtime |
|---|---|---|
| Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 | 1,070Wh | 17.3 hours |
| EcoFlow Delta 3 Max | 2,048Wh | 33.2 hours |
| EcoFlow Delta Pro 3 | 4,096Wh | 2.8 days |
| EcoFlow Delta Pro Ultra | 6,144Wh | 4.1 days |

These estimates assume 85% inverter efficiency and the 35% duty cycle described above.
